To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the proposed method, Graph Neighborhood Attentive Pooling (GRAPHNAP), outperforms all other state-of-the-art NRL methods for node embedding on a wide variety of graph datasets; (2) GRAPHNAP is the first method that learns context-sensitive node representations; (3) the proposed method is robust to noise and is able to learn node representations from incomplete graphs.

we introduce a novel pooling method for graph representation learning, that is, Graph Neighborhood Attentive Pooling (GNAP), and demonstrate that it outperforms state-of-the-art methods on link prediction and ranking tasks.
we propose a novel graph representation learning method that is context-sensitive and that we demonstrate its efficacy in the task of link prediction on real-world datasets.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of learning a low-dimensional representation of a graph that is sensitive to the context of a node.
the problem of learning low-dimensional vector representations of graphs, and we propose a new approach that is context-sensitive and learns a set of representations per node.
the development of NRL techniques that are able to exploit the context-sensitive nature of graphs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the context-sensitive approach is more effective than the context-free approach in the NRL.
context-sensitive methods outperforms the traditional methods, but the latter are more efficient.

we propose a novel graph representation learning scheme that learns context sensitive representation of the nodes.
we have developed a context-sensitive approach for NRL.
we are extending the idea of context-sensitive learning to the domain of graph neural networks and propose an end-to-end trainable model for NRL.

the neighborhood of a node can be used to learn multiple representations of the same node.
